ceq_binders_and_inquisitors.description: The Lancer's Perch doesn't float on its own, and the soldiers don't stay on it by choice. Every Ascendancy Gravity-Binder up there holds the spire in the air, and every Ascendancy Inquisitor holds the soldiers in line. The inquisitors are the reason I didn't put my lance down sooner, and I've hated myself for that every day since. Their camp is on the Lancer's Perch, east of here across the chains. Break both of them, and the Perch starts to come apart from the inside.
ceq_binders_and_inquisitors.accept_text: Take the inquisitors first. Once they fall, the lancers stop looking over their shoulders.

ceq_boars_in_the_rows.description: I planted every Earth seed I carried in the sky soil on the Broad Isle, south-west of the Rest, and something digs them up every night. Every Crystalback Boar on the isle comes down to my rows and roots up whatever I planted, and the Young Crystalback follows along to learn how. I grew forty hectares of tomatoes under glass back home in Westland, and I never once had a pest with crystals on its back. I've eaten exactly one of my blue tomatoes so far, and I'd like to eat another. Keep them out of my garden.
ceq_boars_in_the_rows.accept_text: They're lazy in the morning sun. Go early and you'll catch them sleeping in the furrows.

ceq_check_the_knots.description: The new line's on the second rock, and I can't cross to check it without leaving the main lines untended. If I step away from them, something always goes wrong while I'm gone. Go over the planks from the first rock to the second, here in Tethertown, and look at every knot I tied. If one's slipping, you'll see the rope pale where it's pulled. Come back and tell me they're holding, because I won't sleep until somebody does.
ceq_check_the_knots.accept_text: Don't look down while you cross. Everybody does it once, and then they never do it again.

ceq_counting_whales.description: I count the pod in the Whale Shallows from here every morning, and every week the number's smaller. I spent fifteen years counting humpbacks off Maui, and I know what a shrinking pod looks like. I can only see this side of the cloud from where I stand. Walk out to the rock the whales rub on, then go round to the far side, south-east of here, where the pod turns. Count them from the flukes, and I'll count from here.
ceq_counting_whales.accept_text: Every fluke has its own pattern of scars. Don't count the same one twice.

ceq_eyes_over_the_river.description: The Ascendancy flies scouts over the river from the Lancer's Perch, east of the Rest across the chains. Every Ascendancy Scout Construct carries a crystal plate etched with where it flew and when. I've watched them go over at dawn for a month, and I still can't guess their routes. Bring me those plates, and I'll know where they'll be tomorrow. My skiffs will be somewhere else.
ceq_eyes_over_the_river.accept_text: They fly low over the Broad Isle on the way back. That's the place to catch them.

ceq_forge_elder_ommun.description: I've read the name cut over the biggest anvil at the Silent Forge, and every smith in there faces it. It's Ommun, and the letter after it means elder. Forge-Elder Ommun is still giving that forge its orders, mending golems for a war that ended before my people learned to build. That's a long time to keep working for nobody. Go in and put the old smith to rest.
ceq_forge_elder_ommun.accept_text: If he speaks, it'll be in the strike letter. I'd give a lot to know what he says.

ceq_glass_that_burns.description: I keep my skiffs flying with their crystals hooded so the old wards don't see them, and the hoods are cloth. Cloth slips in a crosswind, and then a skiff lights up like a lamp over the river. The Molten Crystal Elemental at the Silent Forge, on its island west of the Golem Fields, turns cloudy and dull when it cools, and dull is exactly what I'm after. Bring me back the cooled glass. I'll make hoods the wards can't see through.
ceq_glass_that_burns.accept_text: Let it cool on the stone before you pick it up. Hot glass has taken off better fingers than yours.

ceq_hawks_on_the_lines.description: I tied Tethertown's rocks onto the Rest with every rope the Earthborn could find. I did rope access on the towers in Rio, so I know what a line looks like before it goes. Every Gale Hawk off the Broad Isle thinks my ropes are the best perch in the sky, and they pick at them while they sit there. If a line frays, a rock with a house on it drifts off. Thin them out, please, before I'm tying knots in the dark again.
ceq_hawks_on_the_lines.accept_text: They roost on the Broad Isle's cliffs, below us to the south-west. Get them there, not on my lines.

ceq_lances_down.description: I trained half of them myself. Every Perch Lancer on that rest will fire on refugees if the captain says so, because I would have, once. The rest is on the Lancer's Perch, east of this dock across the chains. Go up and break them. I don't want them dead because I hate them. I want them dead because they won't put their lances down.
ceq_lances_down.accept_text: If one of them throws his lance down when you come, let him go. Tell him to walk this way.

ceq_mind_the_gangway.description: I keep the survey's skiff landing here on Crashfall, and I've kept it through worse weather than this. The trouble is the Young Crystalback. Every one on the rock comes down to the landing at night and rubs its crystals on my gangway, and every morning there's a little less gangway. The skiff from Lenswatch is the only way off this rock that doesn't involve a long fall. Chase them off for good.
ceq_mind_the_gangway.accept_text: They come at dusk. Wait by the crates and they'll walk straight past you to the timbers.

ceq_old_goldmane.description: My search parties keep turning back on the Broad Isle, and it's always for the same reason. Old Goldmane is the biggest lion I've ever seen, and he doesn't attack. He just walks behind us in the long grass until somebody loses their nerve, and then we all go home. Whoever lit that fire at the observatory is living out there with him. Make the Broad Isle safe to search.
ceq_old_goldmane.accept_text: He circles to the left before he comes in. I've watched him do it every time.

ceq_old_mouth_of_the_spill.description: The biggest crack in the middle of the Spillway's pool has something living in it. I call it the Old Mouth of the Spill, because that's all anyone's ever seen of it. It drags in eels and crabs, and last night it dragged in a refugee's cart with the mule still tied to it. If the council wants guests walking up to the bridge, the Mouth has to go first. I'll stand well back from the edge while you deal with it, and I won't be ashamed of that.
ceq_old_mouth_of_the_spill.accept_text: Stay out of the water when it surfaces. It pulls anything that's wet.

ceq_other_earthborn.description: The survey kept us at the Annex like guests, and I never met another one of us who wasn't on a scholar's list. Now I'm told there's a whole hamlet of Earth people tied on below this place, and I've been too nervous to walk over the planks. Kaisa Lehtonen runs Tethertown, down the south-west edge of the Rest. Take her this note from me, so she knows I'm coming. Tell her there's a guy from Buenos Aires who'd like to say hello.
ceq_other_earthborn.accept_text: If she asks what I'm like, tell her I'm taller in person.

ceq_out_of_the_cracks.description: The stone under the Spillway's pool is cracked, and something's climbing up out of the cracks. Every Rift Crawler round the pool came out of them, and more come up every night. I've kept this aqueduct for thirty years, and I've never seen the stone open like this. I don't know what's under there, and I don't want to find out by being pulled in. Drive them back down where they came from.
ceq_out_of_the_cracks.accept_text: They come out at the edges of the cracks, not the middles. Stand on solid stone when you fight.

ceq_ringwarden_kozh.description: When I stood under the bells, something in the broken citadel watched me the whole time. It was Ringwarden Kozh, a stone thing as tall as a house, standing at the citadel gate. Today it walked out onto the ring and pushed a pilgrim off the spans, and I watched him fall. Nobody will walk out to the Orbiting Ruins again while it's standing, and that includes me. Go out and bring it down.
ceq_ringwarden_kozh.accept_text: It's slow to turn. Get behind it and stay there, and it'll spend the whole fight looking for you.

ceq_seeds_in_sky_soil.description: Before I spend another seed, I'd like to know what the sky soil actually likes. Sungrass grows wild all over these islands, and nobody up here plants it, it just comes. If it grows next to my tomatoes without choking them, I'll know the two can share a bed. Gather me enough Sungrass to plant a row beside them. If they grow well together, we'll all eat better this winter.
ceq_seeds_in_sky_soil.accept_text: Pull it with the roots on. Sungrass without its roots is just very expensive hay.

ceq_serpents_under_the_pod.description: Every Cloud Serpent in the Whale Shallows swims under the pod and waits for a calf to drift low, and then the Skimming Ray comes in after it. I've watched them take two calves this month. I spent fifteen years telling people not to interfere with nature, and I've decided this isn't my nature. The pod's barely holding its numbers as it is. Keep them off the calves.
ceq_serpents_under_the_pod.accept_text: The rays follow the serpents. Kill a serpent and wait, and the rays come to you.

ceq_sinew_for_rope.description: My ropes are climbing rope and ship rope and one very long extension cord, and they won't last forever. I can't make more of any of them up here. Every Skymane Lion on the Broad Isle, south-west of the Rest, has sinew that'd hold a house. I've seen what a lion's tendon does when it dries, and it's better than anything I hung off in Rio. Bring me some, and I'll braid lines that outlast all of us.
ceq_sinew_for_rope.accept_text: Cut it long, from the hind leg. Short pieces mean knots, and knots mean weak spots.

ceq_something_to_eat.description: Everything we had to eat went over the edge when the skiff came down, and the Rest is already feeding the whole Eighth Ring. I don't want our lot taking bread out of a refugee's bowl. There's a Cloudfleece Ram on every patch of grass down on Crashfall, south-west at the bottom of the river, and I know how to cook one. My grandmother roasted lamb every Sunday in Buenos Aires, and I watched her do it for twenty years. Bring me back some shanks, and I'll feed everyone who walked out of that wreck.
ceq_something_to_eat.accept_text: Take the hind legs, not the front. My grandmother would come back from the dead if I cooked the front.
ceq_something_to_eat.turn_in_text:
Three years up here, and I've learned to cook a sky sheep. My mother would be proud and a little confused.

Eat something while it's hot. The Rest's bread is very good, but it isn't meat.

ceq_spire_captain_alun_vesk.description: Spire-Captain Alun Vesk gave the order I wouldn't follow. He said a parley with refugees was a trick, and he told us to fire. Some of us did, and I put my lance down on the stones and walked. He's still up there, at the top of the watch-spire on the Lancer's Perch, east of here. Go up the spire and finish what I should have started that day.
ceq_spire_captain_alun_vesk.accept_text: Tell him Dace sent you. I want him to know I'm still alive.

ceq_stone_in_the_road.description: The road upriver from Crashfall runs north-east through the Golem Fields, and it's the only way to Halcyon Rest and Aurelion. I've seen the Golem-Field Rubble rolling over it, and I'm sure none of it was moving last month. When my leg holds, I'll be walking that road like the rest of you. I don't want to walk it round rocks that get up and follow me. Break the rubble up so the road stays a road.
ceq_stone_in_the_road.accept_text: Hit the cracks, not the faces. They come apart along the old seams.

ceq_stormwright_yrvald.description: Idris says the light that killed Varo's skiff came from a storm the Kharad bound in a well under the Golem Fields, and that one of them still keeps it. She calls him Stormwright Yrvald. That storm is why my skiffs fly dark with their crystals hooded, and why I lose a pilot every season anyway. The way down is the Deep Stair at the bottom of the Golem Vault, and it ends in the Storm-Well. Go down and put him out, so my skiffs can fly with their lights on again.
ceq_stormwright_yrvald.accept_text: Keep your crystals covered on the stair. The storm looks for anything that shines.

ceq_the_bells_of_the_ring.description: I was at the market when the Eighth Ring fell, and so I lived, and my street didn't. That morning the bells on the Orbiting Ruins rang, west of here, out on the ring. Every Bellringer Sprite out there has rung them every morning since, and I can hear them from my bed in the pavilions. Every morning I wake up thinking it's that morning again. Make them stop, please, so I can wake up in this one.
ceq_the_bells_of_the_ring.accept_text: They dart between the bells. Wait until one lands on a rope and it can't get away fast.

ceq_the_broken_citadel.description: Halcyon Rest has looked out at the Orbiting Ruins for three hundred years, and none of us ever asked who built them. The ruins turn round a broken citadel west of here, across the old causeway from the Broad Isle. If Idris is right about the Kharad, that citadel is theirs. I'd like to know what my grandfathers were drinking tea and looking at all that time. Walk out across the ring, stand in front of the citadel, and tell me if it's cut with the same letters.
ceq_the_broken_citadel.accept_text: The causeway shifts underfoot. Walk it when the ring's turned toward you, not away.

ceq_the_councils_courtesy.description: The council sent me down with a case of gifts and its own seal, to welcome you to Aurelion properly. The case was thrown clear when the skiff came down on Crashfall, south-west at the bottom of the river, and I walked up here without it. The High Houses don't send a guest an invitation without a seal on it. The gifts don't matter, but the seal does. Search the wreck for my seal-case, and I'll try to look less like a man who lost the council's seal.
ceq_the_councils_courtesy.accept_text: It's a blue case with gold corners. If it's open, I don't want to hear about the gifts.
ceq_the_councils_courtesy.turn_in_text:
The gifts are glass now, but the seal's whole. That's the first thing that's gone right today.

I'll keep it in my coat until the road to the bridge is open. When it is, it's yours to carry.

ceq_the_forge_is_warm.description: Idris told me where the golems were made, and I haven't stopped looking west since. The Silent Forge sits on its own island west of the Golem Fields, and there's smoke over it for the first time in anyone's memory. A Forge Guardian stands at every door and an Ancestral Smith works at every anvil. I don't want to find out what they're making down there. Put out the forge's keepers before it's finished.
ceq_the_forge_is_warm.accept_text: Don't stand in the doorways. The guardians were built to fill them, and they hit like it.

ceq_the_heralds_seal.description: The river road is open, the Perch has fallen back and the Silent Forge is cold. That's more than the council ever asked of its guests. Bridgewarden Caldus Rhee holds the foot of the sky-bridge, north of here at the top of the river, past the Spillway. Take the council's seal up to him, and Aurelion's door will open for you. It's your invitation, and I'd like you to deliver it yourself.
ceq_the_heralds_seal.accept_text: Caldus will read every word of it twice. Let him, it's how he's kept the bridge so long.

ceq_the_lancers_perch.description: I served at the Lancer's Perch until I put my lance down, and I walked off it with nothing but my boots. You can see its watch-spire from this dock, east of the Rest across the Ascendancy's chains. I know what used to stand under that spire, and they'll have added to it since I left. Cross the chains and get under the watch-spire. Count the guns, count the tents, and count the lancers on the rest.
ceq_the_lancers_perch.accept_text: Go round the back of the tents, where the cooks dump the ash. Nobody guards the rubbish.

ceq_the_last_few.description: Thirty-one of us woke up on these islands, and I've found twenty-eight. I ran search and rescue out of Rovaniemi, and I don't stop counting until everyone's home. Somebody saw a light in the old observatory on the Broad Isle, south-west of the Rest, and somebody else saw footprints going down to the edge of the Last Falls, right at the bottom of the river. I can't leave Tethertown for long. Search both places, and bring back anything you find, even if it's bad.
ceq_the_last_few.accept_text: If you find a name scratched anywhere, copy it exactly. Spelling matters when you're telling a family.

ceq_the_pale_serpent.description: The biggest serpent in the Whale Shallows is white like the cloud, and you only see it when it moves. I watched The Pale Serpent take a calf in one bite last week, and the mother called for it all night. The pod won't come down low while it's there, and they can't feed up high. Find it in the white and kill it. Don't let it see you first.
ceq_the_pale_serpent.accept_text: Watch the cloud for a ripple that goes against the wind. That ripple is the serpent.

ceq_the_road_from_the_spillway.description: The people of the Eighth Ring walk down the river to us because the city has nowhere else to put them. They come down from the Spillway along the river road. I've lost two of them on the way this month, an old woman and the boy who was helping her. Every Skymane Lion on the Broad Isle, south of the Rest, has learned that the river road is full of tired people. Hunt them, so the next ones who walk down here don't get eaten on the way.
ceq_the_road_from_the_spillway.accept_text: The lions lie up in the long grass by the road. You'll see the grass move before you see them.

ceq_the_sentinels_still_keep_watch.description: The Kharad Sentinel never fell with the golems on the Golem Fields. It stood still with its eyes shut for as long as we've kept records, and now they've opened. Every one has a ward-core in its chest, cut with the strike letter, the same letter as the wards at Crashfall. I want those cores on my table. If I can read the wards, I might be able to tell them to stop.
ceq_the_sentinels_still_keep_watch.accept_text: The cores are hot when they come out. Wrap them in something you don't mind losing.

ceq_the_skiffs_heart.description: The skiff's crystal broke when we hit, and I've been lying here counting what's left of it. Half of it's gone. Every Crashfall Scuttler on this rock has carried a piece off to its hole, because they like anything that shines, even when it's dark. I can't stand yet, but I can still read a crystal if you put it in my hands. Bring me back what they took, and I'll see if there's enough of her heart left to send a signal.
ceq_the_skiffs_heart.accept_text: They hide the pieces under the wreck's plating. Lift it from the edge, it's sharp.

ceq_the_sky_bridge.description: I've got the council's seal, and Aurelion's door is open to you. I've stood guard on this bridge for twelve years, and I've never once let anyone from the ground set foot on it. I turned back a trader last spring who swore he was a magister's cousin. Today the council tells me you're its guest, and I'll take the council at its word. Walk up to the foot of the sky-bridge and look at it.
ceq_the_sky_bridge.accept_text: I want to see what your face does. Most people's go quiet.

ceq_the_sleepers_wake.description: The war-golems came from somewhere, and Idris has found the door to it on the west side of the Golem Fields, downriver to the south-west. She says it goes down into the Golem Vault, where the Kharad kept their golems, and the crews who built them are lying in the stone beside them. They're waking with the golems. Every Vault Sleeper and Thunder-Binder Sleeper that gets up is one more giant between us and Aurelion. I'm curious, and I'm not stupid, so you go first.
ceq_the_sleepers_wake.accept_text: Idris says the binders throw lightning. I'd stay out of the puddles, myself.

ceq_the_unbound_core.description: Something is humming under the great sword in the middle of the Golem Fields, and I've finally worked out what it is. The Unbound Core is Kharad stone round Aetherian-cut crystal, holding a storm the Veyr sang into it, and every time it pulses, another golem stands up. That's three peoples' work in one thing, and nobody in Aurelion will believe it. I've spent my life proving the Kharad were real, and I'd love to study it. I'd love even more to still be alive tomorrow, so break it.
ceq_the_unbound_core.accept_text: Bring me a chip of the casing if one comes loose. Just a chip, I'm not greedy.

ceq_the_wards_were_kharad.description: I've copied the letter the Ward-Sparks leave behind, and it isn't any script my house ever taught me. Scholar Idris Marrowell is lodging here at the Rest, by the dais in the Pool Garden. She's of the House of Long Memory, and she's spent her whole life on the Kharad. My house used to laugh at hers for saying the Kharad built the old stones before we came. Take her this sketch, and tell her I'm sorry we laughed.
ceq_the_wards_were_kharad.accept_text: She'll pretend she isn't pleased. Let her have that, she's earned it.
ceq_the_wards_were_kharad.turn_in_text:
Ilaren Vey sent this, and Ilaren Vey said sorry? I'll have that written down.

It's Kharad, and it's a ward letter, the one that means strike, and it's cut on every golem lying out on the Golem Fields. They're the same makers, and they woke up on the same day.

ceq_they_were_lying_still.description: The House of Long Memory has drawings of the war-golems lying exactly where they fell on the Golem Fields, three hundred years of them. I copied half of them myself as a student. Since the seal cracked, every Waking War-Golem out there has been getting up, and they're all walking downriver toward the wards. The fields are south-west of the Rest, where the river comes off the Broad Isle. Put them back down, and I'll mark where each one falls.
ceq_they_were_lying_still.accept_text: Count how many steps each one took before it went down. I'd like the number.

ceq_vault_thane_brask.description: Idris read the name cut over the wrights' hall in the Golem Vault, where the golems were made. It's Vault-Thane Brask, and he was the vault's keeper. He's awake again and keeping it, with his shield up in the wrights' hall, the way he must have stood a thousand years ago. You don't have to go and fight him. I'd still like to know what a giant thane guards so hard.
ceq_vault_thane_brask.accept_text: The vault's door is on the west side of the Golem Fields. Take a light, Idris says it's dark as a pocket.

ceq_what_brought_us_down.description: I watched the light that hit our skiff come up off the islands, and I've been thinking about it ever since we walked up here. The wreck's still down on Crashfall, south-west at the bottom of the river. Every Ward-Spark round the wreck is a piece of whatever shot us down, and they're still trying to finish the job. Varo can't stand yet, and I won't have them setting the rest of the skiff alight round him. Go down and put them out, and bring me anything they leave behind.
ceq_what_brought_us_down.accept_text: They leave a mark on the stone when they go out. Look for it, because that mark is what I'm after.

ceq_whats_in_the_water.description: This is Aurelion's water, coming down through what's left of the Fourth Aqueduct. It's meant to turn back into the city, clean enough to drink in the High Houses. Since the change, it spills down into the Spillway instead, and every Spillway Eel and Crystal Crab in the Expanse has found it and moved in. I can't see the aqueduct's footings for the creatures in the pool. Clear them out, and I'll be able to see what's wrong.
ceq_whats_in_the_water.accept_text: The crabs hide under the ledge by the falls. Tip the stones and they'll scuttle out.

ceq_word_to_the_wardens.description: The council has sent a second letter, and I'm sorry to say it isn't the welcome you were promised. The anchors hold up the shelf the outer rings are moored to, and they have for a thousand years. One of them is slipping, and the council would rather its first guest from the ground saw to that before a ring drops. Go east along the old aqueduct arm from the Spillway to the Anchorfields. Take this to Warden-Prime Aldric Sorne at Keelstone.
ceq_word_to_the_wardens.accept_text: The bridge will still be here when you get back. I'll make sure of it.

ceq_word_upriver.description: Ilaren, Leandro and the herald went on up the river to Halcyon Rest, and I'm stuck here until my leg holds. The Rest is the waystation halfway up, north-east of Crashfall, past the Golem Fields and across the Broad Isle. Keeper Ithren Lorrow speaks to the council every evening, and he'll believe a crash report more if it comes from the pilot who flew it. I've written it all down, every second of it, lying on my back. Take my letter to the keeper, and he'll send it on tonight.
ceq_word_upriver.accept_text: Don't stop for the scenery. It's lovely, and most of it bites.

ceq_wyrms_on_the_ring.description: I'd like to stand by those bells on the Orbiting Ruins and look at them just once, without hearing them ring. I keep telling myself it'll help, and the keeper says it might. I can't fight, though, and every Ringwind Wyrm out there coils round the spans like they're its own. I sold candles on the Eighth Ring, and the worst thing I ever fought was a stuck wick. Clear them off, and I'll walk out there myself.
ceq_wyrms_on_the_ring.accept_text: They uncoil when they're about to strike. If it straightens, step back.
